questions.question: The price of a phone is increased by 20% and the new price is then decreased by 20%. What is the net change in price?
questions.solution: Net change = a + b + ab/100 = 20 − 20 − (20×20)/100 = −4%, i.e. a 4% decrease.

questions.question: A's salary is 25% more than B's. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's?
questions.solution: Let B = 100, so A = 125. B is less than A by 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

questions.question: If 40% of a number is 96, what is 65% of the same number?
A town's population is 50,000. It grows by 10% in the first year and 20% in the second. What is the population after 2 years?
A student scoring 30% fails by 30 marks. Another student scoring 45% gets 15 marks more than the pass mark. What are the maximum marks?
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its spending on sugar stays the same?
An article bought for ₹800 is sold for ₹1,000. What is the profit percentage?
An item has a marked price of ₹1,200 and is sold at a 15% discount. What is the selling price?
A shopkeeper marks goods 40% above cost price and gives a 10% discount. What is his profit percentage?
Selling an item for ₹1,140 causes a loss of 5%. At what price should it be sold to make a 5% profit?
Two items are each sold for ₹990, one at a 10% profit and the other at a 10% loss. What is the overall result?
A dishonest dealer sells at cost price but uses a 900 g weight in place of 1 kg. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: He gives 900 g but charges for 1000 g. Profit % = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9%.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
What is the difference between compound and simple interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum?
A sum of money doubles in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution: Interest = P in 8 years, so R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.question: A sum becomes ₹8,820 in 2 years at 5% per annum compound interest. What is the principal?
₹1,800 is divided in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest share?
questions.solution: Total parts = 9, so one part = ₹200. Largest share = 4 × 200 = ₹800.

questions.question: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.solution: Make B equal: A:B = 8:12 and B:C = 12:15, so A:B:C = 8:12:15.

questions.question: A and B invest ₹30,000 and ₹45,000 respectively for one year. The profit is ₹15,000. What is A's share?
What is the mean proportional between 9 and 16?
questions.solution: Mean proportional = √(9 × 16) = √144 = 12.

questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7 : 5. When 12 more girls join, the ratio becomes 1 : 1. How many boys are there?
The average of 5 numbers is 20. When one number is removed, the average of the rest is 18. What number was removed?
questions.solution: Sum of 5 = 100. Sum of 4 = 72. Removed = 100 − 72 = 28.

questions.question: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
The average age of 30 students is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average becomes 15 years. What is the teacher's age?
questions.solution: Sum of 30 ages = 420. Sum of 31 ages = 31 × 15 = 465. Teacher = 465 − 420 = 45 years.

questions.question: In what ratio must rice at ₹40/kg be mixed with rice at ₹55/kg to get a mixture worth ₹45/kg?
questions.solution: Alligation: (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1 (cheaper : dearer).

questions.question: A 20-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.solution: Milk = 15 L, water = 5 L. For 3 : 2, water must be 10 L, so add 5 L.

questions.question: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how long will they take?
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: 6 men can finish a piece of work in 10 days. How many days will 15 men take?
questions.solution: Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 man-days. 60/15 = 4 days.

questions.question: A and B together can do a job in 10 days. A alone can do it in 15 days. How long will B take alone?
questions.solution: B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so B takes 30 days.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B empties it in 9 hours. If both are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill?
questions.solution: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/9 = 1/18 per hour, so 18 hours.

questions.question: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 6 days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the job?
questions.solution: In 6 days they do 6 × (1/20 + 1/30) = 1/2 of the job. B does the other 1/2 in 30 × 1/2 = 15 days.

questions.question: A 150 m long train runs at 54 km/h. How long does it take to cross a pole?
A car goes from A to B at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the round trip?
questions.solution: For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 60 × 40/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.question: A 200 m long train running at 72 km/h crosses a 300 m long platform. How long does it take?
A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long does the boat take to go 36 km downstream?
questions.solution: Downstream speed = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h. Time = 36/18 = 2 h.

questions.question: Two trains, 120 m and 180 m long, run in opposite directions at 40 km/h and 50 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance = 300 m. Time = 300/25 = 12 s.

questions.question: How many trailing zeros does 50! have?
questions.solution: Count the factors of 5: ⌊50/5⌋ + ⌊50/25⌋ = 10 + 2 = 12.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2¹⁰ is divided by 7?
What is the HCF of 36 and 84?
What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?
How many positive factors does 360 have?
What is the unit digit of 7⁹⁵?
questions.solution: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat 7, 9, 3, 1. 95 mod 4 = 3, so the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, which is 3.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, what is x² + 1/x²?
If 3x − 7 = 2x + 5, what is x?
If the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0 are a and b, what is a² + b²?
questions.solution: a + b = 5 and ab = 6. a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab = 25 − 12 = 13. (The roots are 2 and 3.)

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 25 and their difference is 7. What is their product?
questions.solution: The numbers are (25 + 7)/2 = 16 and (25 − 7)/2 = 9. Product = 144.

questions.question: If a + b = 7 and ab = 10, what is a³ + b³?
A right triangle has legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the area of its circumcircle?
questions.solution: Hypotenuse = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm. The hypotenuse is the circumdiameter, so r = 5 and area = 25π cm².

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 12 cm long and 8 cm wide?
questions.solution: Perimeter = 2(l + b) = 2(12 + 8) = 40 cm.

questions.question: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.solution: Each interior angle = (n − 2) × 180°/n = 4 × 180/6 = 120°.

questions.question: A cube has a total surface area of 150 cm². What is its volume?
questions.solution: 6a² = 150 ⇒ a = 5 cm. Volume = 5³ = 125 cm³.

questions.question: What is the area of an equilateral triangle with side 6 cm?
If the radius of a circle increases by 10%, by what percentage does its area increase?
questions.solution: Area ∝ r². 1.1² = 1.21, so the area increases by 21%.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word LEVEL be arranged?
questions.solution: 5 letters with L twice and E twice: 5!/(2! × 2!) = 30.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 people sit in a row?
In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
A committee of 3 is chosen from 5 men and 4 women. In how many ways can this be done if it must include at least one woman?
questions.solution: Total = 9C3 = 84. All-men = 5C3 = 10. At least one woman = 84 − 10 = 74.

questions.question: How many diagonals does a regular decagon (10 sides) have?
Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
A card is drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability that it is a king?
questions.solution: There are 4 kings: 4/52 = 1/13.

questions.question: Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least two heads?
questions.solution: Outcomes with 2 or 3 heads: HHT, HTH, THH, HHH, which is 4 of 8, so 1/2.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the product of the numbers is even?
questions.solution: The product is odd only when both are odd: 3 × 3 = 9 outcomes. P(even) = 1 − 9/36 = 3/4.

questions.question:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. Some birds are cats.
questions.solution: Cats ⊂ Dogs ⊂ Birds, so all cats are birds (I). Converting I gives some birds are cats (II). Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: Some pens are books. No book is a pencil.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are not pencils. II. No pen is a pencil.
questions.solution: The pens that are books cannot be pencils, so I follows. Pens that are not books may or may not be pencils, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red.
Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. All flowers are roses.
questions.solution: The red flowers may lie entirely outside the roses, so I is not certain. 'All roses are flowers' does not make all flowers roses, so II fails too.

questions.question:
Statements: No apple is a mango. All mangoes are fruits.
Conclusions: I. Some fruits are not apples. II. No fruit is an apple.
questions.solution: The mangoes are fruits and none of them is an apple, so some fruits are not apples (I). Apples could still be fruits, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: All books are pages. No page is a pen.
Conclusions: I. No book is a pen. II. Some pages are books.
questions.solution: Books ⊂ Pages and Pages ∩ Pens = ∅, so no book is a pen (I). Converting 'all books are pages' gives some pages are books (II).

questions.question:
Statements: Some teachers are doctors. Some doctors are engineers.
Conclusions: I. Some teachers are engineers. II. No teacher is an engineer.
questions.solution: Neither conclusion is definite on its own. But I ('some') and II ('no') are about the same two groups and together cover every case, so exactly one must be true: Either I or II follows (the standard rule for complementary pairs).

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. S is in the middle. R is at one of the extreme ends. T is second from the left. Q is immediately to the right of P. Who sits at the extreme right?
questions.solution: Positions 1–5 from the left: S = 3, T = 2. P and Q need two adjacent free seats, which is only 4–5, so P = 4 and Q = 5, leaving R = 1. Order: R T S P Q.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. S is in the middle. R is at one of the extreme ends. T is second from the left. Q is immediately to the right of P. Who sits exactly between T and P?
questions.solution: The order is R T S P Q, so S sits between T (2nd) and P (4th).

questions.question: Six friends A–F sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B is immediately to the left of A. E is immediately to the right of D. C is not a neighbour of A. Who sits opposite B?
questions.solution: Fix A. D is opposite A. B is A's left neighbour and E is D's right neighbour. C can't sit next to A, so C takes the seat opposite B, and F sits on A's right.

questions.question: Six friends A–F sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B is immediately to the left of A. E is immediately to the right of D. C is not a neighbour of A. Who is immediately to the right of A?
questions.solution: Going clockwise from A (to each person's left): A, B, E, D, C, F. So F is on A's right.

questions.question: Six friends A–F sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B is immediately to the left of A. E is immediately to the right of D. C is not a neighbour of A. Who sits between E and C?
questions.solution: Clockwise order: A, B, E, D, C, F. D sits between E and C.

questions.question: Pointing to a man, Riya says, "He is the son of my father's father's only son." How is the man related to Riya?
questions.solution: Father's father's only son = Riya's father. Her father's son is her brother.

questions.question: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.solution: A and B are C's children and D is C's father. A is female, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.question: X is the wife of Y. Y is the brother of Z. How is X related to Z?
questions.solution: X is married to Z's brother, so X is Z's sister-in-law.

questions.question: P is the father of Q. Q is the mother of R. How is P related to R?
questions.solution: P is the father of R's mother, so P is R's (maternal) grandfather.

questions.question: Introducing a woman, Amit says, "Her mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is Amit related to the woman?
questions.solution: The only daughter of Amit's mother is Amit's sister. The woman's mother is Amit's sister, so Amit is her maternal uncle.

questions.question: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded?
questions.solution: Each letter moves one place forward: C→D, A→B, T→U. So DOG → EPH.

questions.question: In a code, APPLE = 50 (the sum of the letters' alphabet positions). What is GRAPE?
If BOOK is coded as YLLP, how is DESK coded?
questions.solution: Each letter is swapped with its mirror letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, …): B→Y, O→L, K→P. So D→W, E→V, S→H, K→P gives WVHP.

questions.question: In a code, PEN is written as 16-5-14. How is INK written?
questions.solution: Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position: I = 9, N = 14, K = 11.

questions.question: In a language, 'sky is blue' is 'ta na pa', 'blue is nice' is 'na ri ta' and 'nice day' is 'ri lo'. What is the code for 'sky'?
questions.solution: Sentences 1 and 2 share 'is blue' and 'ta na', so {is, blue} = {ta, na}. The word left in sentence 1, 'sky', must be 'pa'.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a 5-floor building (floor 1 is the lowest, floor 5 the top). R lives on an even-numbered floor. Q lives immediately above R. T lives on the top floor. S lives on a floor below P. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.solution: T = 5. R is even: if R = 4 then Q = 5, which is taken, so R = 2 and Q = 3. P and S share floors 1 and 4 with S below P, so S = 1 and P = 4.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a 5-floor building (floor 1 is the lowest, floor 5 the top). R lives on an even-numbered floor. Q lives immediately above R. T lives on the top floor. S lives on a floor below P. Who lives on the lowest floor?
questions.solution: From the solution (S1, R2, Q3, P4, T5), S lives on floor 1.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a 5-floor building (floor 1 is the lowest, floor 5 the top). R lives on an even-numbered floor. Q lives immediately above R. T lives on the top floor. S lives on a floor below P. How many people live between S and T?
questions.solution: S is on floor 1 and T on floor 5. R, Q and P live between them, so 3 people.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a 5-floor building (floor 1 is the lowest, floor 5 the top). R lives on an even-numbered floor. Q lives immediately above R. T lives on the top floor. S lives on a floor below P. Who lives immediately below T?
questions.solution: T is on floor 5 and floor 4 belongs to P.

questions.question: Ana, Ben and Cara each own a different pet: a cat, a dog or a fish. Ana does not own the dog. Ben owns the fish. Who owns the dog?
questions.solution: Ben has the fish, and Ana can't have the dog, so Ana has the cat and Cara has the dog.

questions.question: Ravi walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 9 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.solution: Right of north is east. He ends 3 km east and 9 − 5 = 4 km south of the start. Distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.

questions.question: You face north, turn right, turn right again, and then turn left. Which direction are you facing now?
questions.solution: North → right → East → right → South → left → East.

questions.question: Meena walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 6 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. Where is she now with respect to her starting point?
questions.solution: Left of south is east, and left of east is north. She goes 10 S, then 6 E, then 10 N, so she ends 6 m east of the start.

questions.question: Early in the morning, Rohan stands with his shadow falling exactly to his right. Which direction is he facing?
questions.solution: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall to the west. West is on your right when you face south.

questions.question: A man walks 3 km east, then 4 km north, then 6 km west. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
questions.solution: Net movement: 3 − 6 = 3 km west and 4 km north. Distance = √(9 + 16) = 5 km, towards the north-west.

questions.question: Find the next term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: The terms are n(n + 1): 1×2, 2×3, …, 5×6, so next is 6×7 = 42.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
questions.solution: Each term = previous × 2 − 1, so 33 × 2 − 1 = 65.

questions.question: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ?
Find the next term: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ?
questions.solution: These are consecutive prime numbers. The next prime after 13 is 17.

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 6, 12, 14, 28, 30, ?
Find the next pair: AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.solution: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) and the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W).

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125
questions.solution: 8, 27, 64 and 125 are perfect cubes (2³, 3³, 4³, 5³). 100 is not a cube.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 17, 23, 29, 33, 37
questions.solution: All the others are prime. 33 = 3 × 11.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Rhombus
questions.solution: Square, rectangle and rhombus have four sides. A triangle has three.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 121, 169, 289, 324, 361
questions.solution: 121 = 11², 169 = 13², 289 = 17², 361 = 19² are squares of primes. 324 = 18², and 18 isn't prime.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: ACE, BDF, GIK, MOP
questions.solution: The others skip one letter each time (A_C_E). In MOP the last step, O→P, skips nothing.

questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands at 3:40?
What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at exactly 9:00?
questions.solution: At 9:00 the hands are 3 hour-marks apart: 3 × 30° = 90° (the smaller angle).

questions.question: How many times do the hour and minute hands coincide in 12 hours?
questions.solution: The hands coincide every 12/11 hours, so 11 times in 12 hours. There's no separate meeting between 11 and 1, because that one happens at 12:00.

questions.question: 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday. What day of the week is 1 January 2026?
questions.solution: 2025 is not a leap year: 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.

questions.question: On what day of the week did 15 August 1947 fall?
questions.solution: Odd days up to 1900 = 1. Years 1901–1946 = 46 + 11 leap years = 57 ≡ 1. 1 Jan–15 Aug 1947: 31+28+31+30+31+30+31+15 = 227 ≡ 3. Total = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5, which is Friday (Sunday = 0).

questions.question: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock are the two hands of a clock together?
questions.solution: At 4:00 the minute hand is 20 minute-spaces behind and gains 11/12 of a space per minute. Time = 20 × 12/11 = 21 9/11 minutes past 4.

questions.question: Which letter is 7th from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.solution: A B C D E F G: the 7th letter is G.

questions.question: Which letter is 5th to the right of the 10th letter from the left of the English alphabet?
questions.solution: The 10th letter is J. Five to its right is the 15th letter, O.

questions.question: Which letter is 8th from the right end of the English alphabet?
questions.solution: 8th from the right = (27 − 8) = 19th from the left = S.

questions.question: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order, which letter is 10th from the left?
questions.solution: Reversed, the 10th from the left is the 10th from the right of the normal order: 27 − 10 = 17th letter = Q.

questions.question: If the letters of the word EDUCATION are arranged in alphabetical order, how many letters stay in the same position?
questions.solution: In alphabetical order the letters are A C D E I N O T U. Position by position against E D U C A T I O N: E/A, D/C, U/D, C/E, A/I, T/N, I/O, O/T, N/U. No position matches, so the answer is None.

questions.question: If A > B and B > C, which of these must be true?
questions.solution: A > B > C, so A > C.

questions.question:
Statements: P ≥ Q, Q > R, R = S.
Conclusions: I. P > S II. Q > S
questions.solution: P ≥ Q > R = S gives P > S and Q > S. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: M < N ≤ O, O > P.
Conclusions: I. M < O II. N > P
questions.solution: M < N ≤ O gives M < O. N ≤ O and O > P don't fix how N and P compare, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: X = Y > Z ≥ W.
Conclusions: I. X > W II. Y > W
questions.solution: X = Y > Z ≥ W, so both X > W and Y > W.

questions.question:
Statements: A ≥ B, B ≤ C, C < D.
Conclusions: I. A < D II. B < D
questions.solution: B ≤ C < D gives B < D (II). A ≥ B and B ≤ C point in opposite directions, so A and D can't be compared. I does not follow.

questions.question: In a row of 30 students, Ram is 12th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.solution: Position from the right = 30 − 12 + 1 = 19.

questions.question: Priya is 9th from the top and 16th from the bottom in her class ranking. How many students are in the class?
A is taller than B. C is shorter than B. D is taller than A. Who is the shortest?
questions.solution: D > A > B > C, so C is the shortest.

questions.question: In a row, A is 10th from the left and B is 15th from the right. When they swap places, A becomes 18th from the left. How many people are in the row?
questions.solution: After the swap A is in B's old seat, which is 18th from the left and 15th from the right. Total = 18 + 15 − 1 = 32.

questions.question: Among P, Q, R, S and T: Q earns more than R but less than T. P earns less than R. S earns the most. Who earns the second highest?
questions.solution: S > T > Q > R > P, so T is second.
